# Manage AI resources

Make `.ai/` the source of each requested resource. Read `ai-sync convention` and [resource lifecycle examples](../../../docs/agents/ai-resources.md) when the project layout or a resource format is unclear. Use `ai-sync inventory <project-dir>` before editing to find existing declarations and generated destinations. Identify the source, name, intended agent targets, and whether the request is to add, update, or remove it.

## Route by resource

| Resource | Canonical source | Work to perform |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin | `.ai/plugins.yaml` and optional `.ai/packages/` | Follow the [plugin lifecycle](../../../docs/agents/plugin-lifecycle.md) and `ai-sync plugins` commands. Keep the declaration, inspected package, and native installation state distinct. |
| Skill | `.ai/skills/<name>/` | Copy or update the complete skill directory, including referenced scripts and assets. Check `SKILL.md` frontmatter and relative links. Removing it means deleting its canonical directory. |
| Rule | `.ai/rules/<name>.md` | Use YAML `paths` frontmatter for path-scoped guidance. Put repo-wide guidance in `.ai/project.md` and agent-only guidance in `.ai/targets/<target>.md`. Preserve the rule's intent when adapting source globs. |
| MCP server | `.ai/mcp.yaml` under `servers` | Record a local `command` or remote HTTP `url`; use `bearer_token_env_var` for bearer auth and nonsecret `headers` when needed. See [MCP examples](../../../docs/agents/ai-resources.md#mcp-server). Remove the named entry to uninstall its generated configuration. |

For an external source, inspect its actual files and installation requirements before copying or adapting it. Keep provenance available in the canonical resource or accompanying documentation. Do not treat a plugin-provided skill or MCP server as a standalone resource unless the user specifically wants to maintain it independently of the plugin.

## Verify and generate

1. Run `ai-sync inventory <project-dir>` after editing. Resolve diagnostics and check the intended resource's sources and destinations. For skills, confirm supporting files appear with the skill; for rules, inspect the Codex destination because glob scoping can map to a parent directory.
2. Run `ai-sync --dry-run` from the project to review generated changes. It also previews setup and Claude plugin actions; inspect `.ai/setup.yaml` and `.ai/plugins.yaml` when those actions appear.
3. Run `ai-sync` from the project, then check `ai-sync inventory <project-dir>` and the affected generated files. For plugins, also verify native installation through the plugin workflow. For an MCP server, check that the target agent can start or reach it when the environment allows.

If a requested MCP transport or authentication method cannot be represented by the current schema, identify the unsupported part explicitly. Keep the canonical configuration valid and report the remaining target-specific step rather than editing generated files as a hidden workaround.
